# A node's style, drawn by gtk4.
#
# gtk4 read no field of a style but `flex`, so a styled label drew as a plain
# one. `plain` and `styled` write the same text, the second with a size, a
# face, colors and padding; `flips` writes no style, then the same one held
# in a var. testdata/gtk4_style.txtar shows the calls, and
# pkg/go/gtk4rt/look_test.go measures what GTK lays out of them.
#
# Confirmed by reverting the gtk4 change: each pair of snapshots was then the
# same picture.

env SNGL_UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS=1
sngl test --platform=gtk4 app.sngl
stdout 'PASS'
! stdout 'FAIL'
exists app.sngl.snapshots/plain.png
! cmp app.sngl.snapshots/plain.png app.sngl.snapshots/styled.png
! cmp app.sngl.snapshots/before.png app.sngl.snapshots/after.png

-- app.sngl --
import test "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"

output { go { gtk4 } }

const look = ui.Style{width=300px, padding=12px, fontSize=24px, fontWeight=bold, color=#ffffff, background=#335599, borderRadius=8px}

component plain ui.node {
    ui.vbox {
        ui.text(value="styled")
    }
}

component styled ui.node {
    ui.vbox {
        ui.text(value="styled", style=look)
    }
}

component flips ui.node {
    var s = ui.Style{}
    ui.vbox {
        ui.text(value="styled", style=s)
        ui.button #flip(text="flip", @click { s = look })
    }
}

func testPlain(t test.Test, c plain) {
    t.snapshot("plain")
}

func testStyled(t test.Test, c styled) {
    t.snapshot("styled")
}

func testFlips(t test.Test, c flips) {
    t.snapshot("before")
    c.flip.click()
    t.snapshot("after")
}

ui.window {
    styled
}
